text:
maria: Heads-up: after the kernel-selection PR landed I’m seeing a ~12% tail-latency regression on multi-GPU 70B runs. Profiling attached (perf-bot), but opening thread for quick triage.
ajay: ugh. which PR number? any CI artifacts? :thinking_face:
maria: PR 3f2c9b6 — it prefers the new fused attention-softmax kernel when seq_len>512. Perf-bot posted a flamegraph to the perf bucket: s3://redwood-perf/1871234567/trace.html
oliver: quick skim — looks like all-reduce overlaps got worse. AR wall time increased despite compute kernel being slightly faster. suspect more kernel launches blocking the stream.
sarah: can you paste the short profile? numbers help.
perf-bot: Summary from latest profile (70B, bs=8, tp=2, pp=2):

```
compute_total: 210ms -> 196ms (opt kernel)
allreduce_total: 78ms -> 120ms (after PR)
kv_fetch: 14ms -> 18ms
end_to_end_p95: 420ms -> 472ms
```
note: arrows are before->after PR
ajay: wow AR jumped a lot. any change to NCCL config or async/allreduce batching?
maria: NCCL settings unchanged. The fused kernel increases number of small kernels per layer (launch granularity changed). hypothesis: more kernel launches reduce CUDA stream concurrency and prevent NCCL from overlapping compute.
oliver: makes sense. TP shards trigger frequent small allreduces per-head slice, so launch overhead matters. with PP we also have bubbles but fewer AR ops concentrated at stage boundaries.
sarah: this ties into KV cache sharding too. current default: DP replicate KV cache (one copy per GPU) for simplicity. That makes DP memory heavy but minimizes cross-GPU fetches. But TP/PP hybrids change the tradeoffs.
ajay: notes from yesterday’s microbench: when KV is sharded across TP (head-slicing), we see increased AR ops (per-step KV exchange) but much smaller messages. latency suffers for small-message AR.
maria: proposed immediate experiments:
- run bench with `--tp 4 --pp 1 --bs 4` vs `--tp 2 --pp 2 --bs 8` and capture step-level AR counts
- revert kernel selection to previous fused-matmul-softmax for an A/B
- try NCCL_ASYNC=1 + single-stream batching to see overlap effect
oliver: I can run the two configs. command I'll use:
```
./bench/run_profile.sh --model 70B --tp 4 --pp 1 --bs 4 --trace nvtx --out /tmp/trace
./bench/run_profile.sh --model 70B --tp 2 --pp 2 --bs 8 --trace nvtx --out /tmp/trace2
```
will push traces to perf-bot when done.
sarah: longer-term: consider a hybrid KV sharding policy that picks between TP-slice, PP-layer, and DP-replicate based on two signals: message-size vs AR-count and memory headroom. For example:
- if memory headroom low -> prefer TP-shard (saves mem) but switch to larger aggregation to reduce AR count
- if small-message AR dominant -> prefer PP-localization per-layer (move KV to stage owner) to avoid many small allreduces
ajay: +1. Also we should add a kernel-selection cost model that estimates launch overhead impact on NCCL overlap. right now selector optimizes only FLOPS and numeric error.
maria: agreed. Today’s actionable:
1) oliver runs the two benches and uploads traces (assigned: oliver)
2) ajay will roll back kernel selector on a canary build and run p95 comparison (assigned: ajay)
3) sarah + maria to draft KV sharding decision matrix (assigned: sarah, maria)
please react with :thumbsup: if assigned.
oliver: started bench 1 now, ETA ~18m. pushing NVTX trace to s3 on finish.
ajay: rolling back selector to commit 2a4b.. starting canary run now.
perf-bot: nvprof trace uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/1871234567/trace-oliver-1.nvtx
maria: thanks — once we have both traces I’ll run the flamegraph diff and look at kernel launch counts + stream stalls. Also check for unexpected CPU-side stalls (host-side enqueue).
sarah: small note: for PP-native setups we should check micro-batch size per stage. pipeline bubble rate might interact with KV fetch latency and make small AR spikes.
ajay: if rollback proves perf is fine, we should change kernel selector to include a heuristic: if estimated AR_count > X and msg_size < Y -> avoid kernel that increases launch granularity.
maria: good idea. let's capture AR_count and avg_msg_size in the bench outputs. add to bench flags: `--emit-comm-stats`.
oliver: uploaded second trace. links:
- s3://redwood-perf/1871234567/trace-oliver-1.nvtx
- s3://redwood-perf/1871234567/trace-oliver-2.nvtx
ajay: canary rollback results: end_to_end_p95 back to 418ms, allreduce_total down to 80ms. I’ll post diff in perf channel.
maria: OK that nails it to kernel launch/granularity. next steps then:
- ajay: implement selector heuristic (small patch) -> perf test
- sarah/maria: draft KV sharding matrix and add to roadmap for Optimize feature (to suggest default per workload)
- oliver: add `--emit-comm-stats` to bench and re-run sweep
any timeline thoughts? two sprints for selector + bench? two more for KV policy prototyping?
sarah: sounds reasonable. I’ll schedule a short design sync tomorrow 11am PT. invite sent.
maria: thanks team. logging final note: regression root cause = kernel that reduced compute but increased kernel launch count -> reduced comm/compute overlap -> increased AR wall time in TP-heavy configs. Ticket created: PERF-7832. :white_check_mark:
